The '''2006 World Championship''' was the 11th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] on 19–22 October 2006 at PasTimes, a game store in Niles, Illinois, near Chicago.<ref name="f12542">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=12542 Day 3 Results], mc9457, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, "[FY06] Worlds Weekend 2006" (23 October 2006). The forum header reads "October 19th - October 22nd / PasTimes; 8351 1/2 Golf Road; Niles, Illinois 60714".</ref><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref> It had been planned for August 2006; in June the Players Committee reported that PasTimes was working with it on a new date because the August date conflicted with other events.<ref name="pc-jun06">[http://www.swccgpc.com/ SWCCGPC.com] (home page; news item "World's Date Change - Your Vote Matters", admin_mike, 16 June 2006: "PasTimes in Chicago is working with us in order to provide a new date. August date conflicted with other pre-planned events."). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617215932/http://www.swccgpc.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> Wikipedia gives a field of 34.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (World Championship table)</ref> [[Nate Meeker]] topped the twelve-player Day 3 standings on differential and then beat [[Brian Hunter]] in a two-game final, losing game 1 by 1 and winning game 2 by 3.<ref name="f12542" /><ref name="awards" /> Meeker posted his Day 3 Dark deck, "Scum Solid", on DeckTech, but that list was not archived and is not on the wiki.<ref name="f12556">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=12556 Players at Worlds (Post all decklist links here)], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums (24 October – November 2006)</ref>

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal: [[Premiere - Original VS6]], since Virtual Sets 7–11 became legal only on 4 December 2006 (see [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]).

== Results ==

Places 1–2 are from the final; places 3–12 follow the Day 3 standings posted by the Players Committee on 23 October 2006.<ref name="f12542" /> A 2020 forum post quoting an earlier player compilation gives the same standings.<ref name="f75427-1300387">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300387#p1300387 Post by Yoshi], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300387 Internet Archive]</ref> Chris Shaner is also described as "third place overall" in a players' thread.<ref name="f12551">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=12551 What did you play?], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums (24 October 2006)</ref> Decks are the lists recovered in 2026 from DeckTech posts (Internet Archive copies) and Players Committee decklist forms; each deck page cites its own source.

The Players Committee posts spell "Bobby Hilbun"; his decklist is filed under [[Bobby Hilburn]].

=== Top 8 bracket ===

There was no elimination bracket: Day 3 was played as standings among twelve players, and the top two met in a two-game final.<ref name="f12542" /> Individual Day 3 game results were not published.

* Final, game 1: Brian Hunter (Dark) beat Nate Meeker (Light) by 1
* Final, game 2: Nate Meeker (Dark) beat Brian Hunter (Light) by 3

The Players Committee announced Meeker as the 2006 World Champion.<ref name="f12542" />
